- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.35+), as models tend to overreact.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.0+), particularly in the 10-15 day horizon, suggesting mean reversion or panic-driven correction.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or mildly negative; true outcomes often show mean reversion or consolidation.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overpredict 30-day horizon; reduce forecast by 1-2% for each day of sustained positive sentiment.
- If last 3-5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overshoots by 2-5% in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction of 1.5-3% for those periods.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 1-3% for 3-5 days after negative sentiment spikes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate; apply 1-2% downward adjustment if sentiment is < 0.30.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1-2% for 3-5 days after negative sentiment.
